paper.title: MEMRES: A Memory-Augmented Resolver with Confidence Cascade for Agentic Python Dependency Resolution
paper.central_claim: A six-level deterministic-first confidence cascade and self-evolving cross-snippet memory resolve86.6% of HG2.9K, substantially outperforming PLLM while reducing LLM calls and latency.

provenance.notes: Assigned model type sonnet -> gpt-6.1-sol; no independently verifiable model/session receipt available. Blind boundary maintained; no other seat/attempt read.

sections_read: all available text through footer; no appendices present

evidence.quote: 33% are SyntaxErrors from Python 2 code run under Python 3
evidence.support_explanation: Error taxonomy motivates deterministic treatment rather than an LLM for every snippet.

evidence.quote: we emulate this by caching solutions proven successful for earlier code blocks
evidence.support_explanation: Retained successful cases reused across later snippets within the same batch.

evidence.quote: it independently resolves these near-duplicates without relying on batch order, though at a higher runtime cost.
evidence.support_explanation: Author claims removing session memory only changes runtime; Table 2 instead shows lower success.

evidence.quote: Shortcuts are validated with a quick Docker build to prevent compounding errors.
evidence.support_explanation: Executable write gate, not marginal-utility validation.

evidence.quote: Memory is fully reset between independent evaluation runs: no state persists across runs, preventing cross-run overfitting.
evidence.support_explanation: Retention is within-run only, not cross-run deployment learning.

evidence.quote: The first level returning a valid version terminates the cascade
evidence.support_explanation: Deterministic fast-path precedence, no calibrated probabilistic confidence.

evidence.quote: We aggregate 10 independent test runs with randomized snippet orderings

evidence.support_explanation: Table gives 2357/2890=81.6% without Level1 vs2503/2890=86.6%, a146-snippet gain.

evidence.quote: Runtime passes (correct dependencies but environmental failures such as missing display servers or hardware) are counted as failures to prevent inflation.
the 50-entry held-out subset is disjoint from HG2.9K.
evidence.support_explanation: Author states development KB separation, no independent audit.

evidence.quote: these are derived solely from PyPI query results and Docker build signals, not from HG2.9K ground-truth labels
evidence.support_explanation: Test-stream adaptation uses execution feedback rather than target labels.

evidence.quote: Median resolution is 15.2 s for successes.
evidence.support_explanation: Latency conditioned on success; no complete failed-run/update ledger.

evidence.quote: We directly compare against the reported 54.7% success rate from the original PLLM paper
evidence.support_explanation: Historical baseline rather than matched local rerun.
Table1 reports2503±9.3 successes across10 runs; no ablation uncertainty or paired significance.
Repeated runtime-only assertion contradicted by Table2 success loss.

signatures.operation: Try session memory→static map→templates→cooccurrence→heuristics→LLM; first valid version wins; inject apt dependencies and retry builds
signatures.conditions: Known import mappings and version support

signatures.persistence: Runtime mappings retained; most rules static

gap.checked_gap: Concrete error taxonomy and deployment bottleneck, but closest-prior delta is integration of known maps, build search and memory; original neighbors unavailable.

gap.method_response: Explicit repair routes with cached validated pins and bounded fallback.
gap.remaining_gap: Cannot attribute31.9pp historical system gap to memory; only5pp Level1 delta supplied, with contradictory runtime-only narrative.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Executable-validated earlier solutions retained within a batch improve later related-snippet resolution in theLevel1OFFcontrast. No independent frozen-store/cross-run transfer or improver-level evidence.
unresolved: Contradictory accuracy-vs-runtime claims; historical baseline; exact tip/update interfaces not given; no independent reproduction.

E.causality.reason: Memory-off provides scoped attribution, but rest ofcascade not isolated and historical baseline unmatched.

E.holdout.reason: Declared disjoint static development and run resets; learned cases share same evaluation stream and near duplicates, no independent frozen-store corpus.

E.statistics.reason: Ten shuffled runs and std9.3; no paired ablation interval or significance; meets repeated-run evidence but not3+ criteria.

E.cost.reason: Calls, latency and hardware reported; failed/retried builds, memory maintenance and full matched baseline ledger absent.

reason: Complete material supports a scoped same-session retained-memory result; methodological contradictions and controls graded as author-side limitations.
